data: © CNSA. Sample mass 1.731 kg returned to Earth 2020-12-16; first lunar samples since Luna 24 (1976).
中国探月与深空探测网 (CLEP)
嫦娥五号 — 中文维基百科

First lunar sample return in 44 years — ending a gap since Luna 24 (1976). Returned 1.731 kg from a geologically young region (2 billion years old vs 3–4 billion for Apollo samples). Rewrote our model of lunar volcanism: the Moon was geologically active much more recently than thought.
Modern robotic sample return architecture — direct precursor to Mars Sample Return's lander/ascent vehicle/orbiter chain.

Chang'e 5 landed in Mons Rümker on December 1, 2020 — China's first lunar sample-return mission and the first lunar sample return by any nation since Luna 24 (1976), 44 years earlier. Returned 1,731 g of samples from young volcanic terrain (~2 billion years old, compared to ~3.5 Ga Apollo samples), proving that lunar volcanism continued far later than previously known.
Chang'e 5 stack — four-element vehicle: lander/ascender (surface), orbiter (lunar rendezvous), reentry capsule (Earth return).
Drill + scoop subsystem — collected samples from both the surface and 1+ m depth.
Long March 5 launches Chang'e 5 — China's most ambitious lunar mission to that point, fully automated 23-day round trip.
Chang'e 5 on the surface near Mons Rümker — 19 hours of operations before ascent stage liftoff.
2-billion-year-old lunar volcanism rewrites Moon thermal history
Sample return capsule on the snow in Inner Mongolia, December 17 2020 — 1,731 g of young basalt back on Earth.
